questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the location (boarders the Atlantic Ocean), the fact that there are many social and outdoor activities (surfing, outdoor climbing, hiking etc), the beautiful city of Lisbon!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my stay and fell in love with both the city and the people. The university was okay too. I took some great courses, along with a few that were less well-structured. Be aware that the process of finding, choosing and organizing your courses at the beginning of the Erasmus can be quite confusing, and that it is not uncommon to encounter an old-fashioned teacher with rather traditional principles...

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to find the information I needed, though I did face some challenges because the deadlines at KU and the Portuguese university did not align.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university has an international office that helped me reorganize some of my courses when I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It worked out okay, but you had to be quite proactive to get everything sorted.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started my search early and found an apartment in a great area via the website Idealista. I'd definitely recommend it, since it's safe and geared toward exchange students like os.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city's metro system works very well, so you can easily live "far" from the university without any trouble. I would personally recommend the neighborhoods of Santos, Principe Real and Chiado.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy to find accommodation, but a bit expensive in the nice areas.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As told, I did face some challenges because the deadlines at KU and the Portuguese university did not align. And I had to be quite proactive to get everything sorted. But the international office helped me out, and it all worked out at the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the beginning not very successful, since some of the classes I was registred for did not exist. But eventually, it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Follow the steps and instructions in the introductory mail, and make sure that you meet the deadlines. 
Be patient with both the Danish and Portuguese university, as the process is pretty slow in the beginning. 
Expect that you might need to change a course or two when you arrive at Lisbon, because their system is not always fully up to date. 
Also, don't hesitate to send them an email if you have any questions about your registration, courses or the Online Learning Agreement . They are very helpful and pretty fast at answering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I enjoyed some of the courses, others not as much. 
There weren't many obvious options for a rhetoric student, so I had to try some new academic fields, such as history and philosophy. This was both exciting and challenging, as it required me to learn and adapt to different - and sometimes conflicting - ways of thinking. 

I would have been more enthusiastic about the program if it hadn't been for the fact that some of my instructors were unstructured and uninspiring in their teaching. One them was even oppressive and openly unpleasant to his students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level wasn't very high, but I still had to keep up most of my courses to avoid loosing track.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In general, there was much less reading and preparation for the courses than at KUA. Being physically present was more valued, and in several courses attendance was part of the assessment. 

I would probably describe the teaching style as quite traditional and not particularly creative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History and Culture of the US (Colonial period - 1900) 
The Study of Cultures
Philosophy of Art (Art and Science)
Human Language Systems 
Language and Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Content-wise, I would recommend the US History course and Human Language Systems, as they were the ones I found most interesting.

If you prefer a lighter workload, I would instead suggest Philosophy of Art and Language and Communication, as they were easier to keep up with and therefore easier to skip from time to time.

I definitely wouldn’t recommend Culture Studies, even though it sounds interesting. The instructor was terrible, which made the classes almost unbearable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn’t really use the school’s non-academic opportunities, so I’m not very familiar with them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend surfing. There’s a really good beginner spot about 30 minutes from the city center (Carcavelos), where you can get a great monthly deal for equipment rental and lessons.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
o to Nazare and watch the big waves 

Take a hiking trip to Sintra 

Go to Fabrica Braco de Prata (a cultural house with live music, beers and different events)

Surf :)

Beginner surfing spots: Carcavelos, Caparica, Baleal (weekend-trip)
More advanced surfing sports: Guincho, Ericeira (weekend-trip)

Outdoor climbing spots (for all levels): Guia Lighthouse (Cascais)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, though I ended up meeting mostly people from other countries.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the classes and explore some of the more local bars and culture houses around town.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Definitely their laid-back and stress-free lifestyle. 

And their tradition of eating out and lingering at cafés.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Lisbon is a safe, beautiful and lovely city to live in.
2) Go on weekendtrips and explore the beautiful nature around Lisbon. Use Flixbus or rent a car (or a van). It’s easy and affordable.
3) Be aware that school takes up quite a bit of your time. Possibly a bit more than you’d expect from an exchange program.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make use of the school’s international office if you have any problems. Their email is: internacional@
letras.ulisboa.pt

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
New friends and hoboes :)

Cheap coffee and authentic food experiences.

Beautiful sunsets and nature experiences :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for and be enrolled in all my courses... 

The Pre-approval and Online Learning Agreement Process... Be patient :))

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Portugal is amazing :)) 

Go on exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
